stred: goes at a pace neither side sets alone
q: I have drawn Isa. How does it come into this?
text: Isa is the other side stopping. Your pace was never yours to set alone, so when the ice comes it sets it for both of you: the ford freezes, the far bank goes quiet, and the going waits at the edge. You could cross on the ice and call the pace shared. It would not be; one side has gone still. The ford lies white from bank to bank, and nothing on it moves at a speed of its own.

stred: whatever he leans on has to lean back the same amount
q: I have drawn Jera. How does it come into this?
text: Jera is a field that leans back slowly. You put your weight into it in spring — the digging, the seed, the hours bent over the rows — and the field takes it without answering for months. Then, late in the year, it leans back, and the rows stand heavy where there was only turned earth. The leaning was matched. It came back in a different season from the one you gave it in, so for a long while it looked like leaning on nothing.

stred: what goes out from him and what comes back are the same weight
q: I have drawn Perth. How does it come into this?
text: Perth is the part still out. Something left your hands — a word, a decision, an offer — and has not come back. What goes out of you and what returns are meant to weigh the same, but this went where you cannot see, and until it returns there is nothing to weigh it against. The scales stand with one pan down and the other empty, waiting on something already on its way that has not said how heavy it is.

stred: never forces and never coasts — whatever carries him, he carries back
q: I have drawn Gebo — my own rune. How does it come into this?
text: Gebo drawn onto your own going is a second walker at your side, going the same way you go — never pressing ahead, never content to be towed. Two walkers built like that keep a very even gap. The space between their shoulders stays the same width for a long stretch of road, and neither of them is the one holding it there. When one slows, the other finds it has slowed too, without having decided to.
